can_do.text: I can say my name, where I'm from, where I live and what I do.
I can ask others the same questions, choosing informal or formal address.
I can say which languages I speak and how well.

checkpoint.text: Introduce yourself to a new colleague in 6–8 sentences, then write 3 questions for them; ask one of them formally.

can_do.text: I can talk about my family and the people close to me.
I can describe someone's appearance and character.
I can say how someone feels right now, as opposed to what they are like in general.

checkpoint.text: Describe two people close to you in 8–10 sentences: appearance, character, and how they are doing this week.

can_do.text: I can ask what something costs and understand and say prices.
I can tell and ask the time and say when something happens.
I can say dates, birthdays and phone numbers.

checkpoint.text: Write out in words 5 prices, 3 times and 2 dates from a given list, then answer 3 questions about when things happen in your week.

can_do.text: I can ask where a place is and understand a simple answer.
I can say what there is in my neighbourhood and where.
I can give and follow simple directions.

checkpoint.text: Describe your neighbourhood (what is there and where), then explain the way from your home to a nearby café in 4–5 steps.

can_do.text: I can describe my typical day with times.
I can say what I am doing right now.
I can say how often I do things.

checkpoint.text: Describe a typical weekday and a typical Sunday (8–10 sentences) with times and frequency words, then add 2 sentences about what you are doing right now.

can_do.text: I can say what my job is, where I work and what I do there.
I can say what I like and dislike about my work and give a simple reason.
I can say what I can, want and prefer to do.

checkpoint.text: Write a short message to a new team member: your role, a normal working day, one thing you like about the job and one you don't, with reasons (6–8 sentences).

can_do.text: I can order food and drinks for myself and others.
I can ask what is in a dish and ask for a change.
I can ask for the bill and pay.
I can say what I usually eat and what I don't eat.

checkpoint.text: Write a café dialogue between you and a waiter (8–10 lines): order for two, ask about one ingredient, change something, ask for the bill.

can_do.text: I can ask for an item in a size or colour and ask the price.
I can compare two items in simple terms.
I can say which one I'll take, or that I'll leave it.

checkpoint.text: Write a shop dialogue (8–10 lines): ask for an item in your size and colour, compare two options with 'this/that', decide, and refer back to the item with a pronoun.

can_do.text: I can talk about my hobbies and sports.
I can say what I and other people like and dislike.
I can agree and disagree with someone's taste (me too / me neither).
I can say what I know how to do and whom or what I know.

checkpoint.text: Write about your free time: 3 things you like, 2 you don't, what a friend likes; then react to 3 given statements with 'me too / me neither / I do / I don't'.

can_do.text: I can talk about my plans for the weekend or the coming days.
I can suggest a time and place to meet, accept, decline and offer an alternative.
I can talk about the weather and what I'll do depending on it.

checkpoint.text: Write a chat with a friend: propose a meeting, decline one time and offer another, agree; then describe your weekend plans including one 'if it rains, ...'.

can_do.text: I can say what I did yesterday or last week.
I can tell someone about my weekend in a few connected sentences.
I can say when something happened.

checkpoint.text: Describe yesterday and last weekend (10–12 sentences) using at least 6 different verbs, including irregular ones (to go, to do, to have).

can_do.text: I can plan a trip and book tickets and accommodation.
I can tell someone about a trip I took.
I can say how, why and for whom I do something.

checkpoint.text: Tell about a past trip (about 10 sentences: how you got there, where you stayed, what you did), then outline your next trip in 3–4 sentences.

can_do.text: I can say what I have done today or this week.
I can ask and answer whether someone has ever done something.
I can say what is already done and what is not done yet.

checkpoint.text: Write an end-of-day message to a colleague: what is done, what is not done yet; then 3 'have you ever...?' questions with your own answers.

can_do.text: I can describe how things used to be and what I used to do.
I can compare the past with the present.
I can describe the background situation of a past event.

checkpoint.text: Compare your life ten years ago with now (10–12 sentences): habits, place, work, free time.

can_do.text: I can describe symptoms and say since when I have had them.
I can understand simple advice and give it to others.
I can ask for help in an urgent situation.

checkpoint.text: Write a pharmacy or doctor dialogue: describe 2–3 symptoms and since when, receive and repeat back 3 pieces of advice; then give a friend 3 tips using commands.

can_do.text: I can describe where I live and its pros and cons.
I can explain that something is broken or not working.
I can ask someone to do or bring something, and say whose something is.

checkpoint.text: Write a message to your landlord: what is broken, since when, what you need; then give a flatmate 3 instructions that refer back to objects with pronouns.

can_do.text: I can write a short work message or email.
I can reschedule a meeting and explain why.
I can explain a task and say what will happen next.

checkpoint.text: Write an email that reschedules a meeting, gives the reason, proposes two new slots and describes next steps.

can_do.text: I can compare options and say which one is the best.
I can give my opinion with a reason.
I can agree or disagree with someone's opinion.

checkpoint.text: Compare two cities, phones or series in 8–10 sentences, pick the best one and justify it; then respond to one opposing opinion.

can_do.text: I can politely complain and ask for a solution.
I can make polite requests.
I can report what someone told me.

checkpoint.text: Write a complaint dialogue at a hotel or restaurant: describe the problem, politely request a solution, then tell a friend what the staff said.

can_do.text: I can tell my life story with key dates.
I can narrate an event: the situation, what happened, how it ended.
I can link events in time (when, while, after, ago, since).

checkpoint.text: Write 150–200 words about an important period or event in your life: when and where, what the situation was, what happened, how it ended.

topics.title: Subject pronouns
topics.summary: yo, tú, él/ella/usted, nosotros/as, vosotros/as, ellos/ellas/ustedes. Usually dropped because the verb ending shows the person; used for emphasis or contrast.
traps: Overusing pronouns sounds unnatural: 'Yo trabajo. Yo vivo...'
usted/ustedes take third-person verb forms.

topics.title: ser: present tense
topics.summary: soy, eres, es, somos, sois, son. Identity, origin, profession, nationality, characteristics.
traps: No indefinite article before an unqualified profession: 'Soy ingeniero', not 'Soy un ingeniero'.

topics.title: Noun gender and plural
topics.summary: Every noun is masculine or feminine. -o usually m., -a usually f., -ión/-dad f. Plural: -s after a vowel, -es after a consonant.
traps: Gender often differs from German/Russian: el coche (das Auto), la leche (die Milch), el problema.

transfer.ru: Род не совпадает с русским в большом числе слов.

topics.title: Definite and indefinite articles
topics.summary: el/la/los/las; un/una/unos/unas. Definite article also for general statements and likes: Me gusta el café.
examples: Un café y una tostada, por favor.
traps: General statements need the definite article where German/English have none: 'La vida es bella'.

transfer.ru: В русском артиклей нет: их легко пропустить, особенно после gustar.

topics.title: Question words
topics.summary: qué, quién, dónde, de dónde, cuándo, cómo, cuánto/a/os/as, por qué, cuál. Always written with an accent; questions open with ¿.
traps: cuánto agrees with the noun: cuántas personas.
qué vs cuál: '¿Cuál es tu número?'

topics.title: Negation with no
topics.summary: no goes directly before the verb (and before object pronouns).
traps: Not after the verb as in German: 'Hablo no' is wrong.

topics.title: Formal address: usted
topics.summary: usted/ustedes = formal 'you', with third-person verb forms and su/sus. In Spain tú is used widely, usted with strangers of authority or older people.
traps: Possessive is su, not tu: '¿Es su maleta?'

topics.title: Adjective agreement
topics.summary: Adjectives agree with the noun in gender and number and usually follow it. -e/-consonant adjectives have one form for both genders.
traps: Agreement with the noun's gender, not with the speaker's: 'la reunión es larga'.

topics.title: Possessive adjectives
topics.summary: mi/mis, tu/tus, su/sus, nuestro/a/os/as, vuestro/a/os/as. They agree with the thing possessed, not the owner.
traps: su is his/her/their/your(formal): ambiguity is resolved by context or 'de él'.
No reflexive 'own' as in Russian «свой»: 'mi billete'.

transfer.ru: «Свой» переводится по лицу: я — mi, ты — tu, он — su.

topics.title: tener: present tense
topics.summary: tengo, tienes, tiene, tenemos, tenéis, tienen. Possession, age (tengo 39 años), physical states (tengo hambre).
traps: Age with tener, not ser: 'Tengo 40 años'.

topics.title: estar: present tense
topics.summary: estoy, estás, está, estamos, estáis, están. Temporary states and location.
traps: Accent on está/están distinguishes from esta/estas.

topics.title: ser vs estar
topics.summary: ser: identity, origin, character, time, where an event takes place. estar: location of things/people, current state, result.
examples: Es simpático, pero hoy está cansado.
La reunión es a las cinco.
traps: Events: 'La fiesta es en mi casa' (ser).
Some adjectives change meaning: ser aburrido / estar aburrido.

topics.title: muy vs mucho
topics.summary: muy + adjective/adverb; mucho/a/os/as + noun (agrees); mucho after a verb (invariable).
traps: 'muy mucho' does not exist; 'muchas gracias' agrees.

topics.title: Numbers 0–29
topics.summary: 0–15 individual words; 16–19 and 21–29 written as one word: dieciséis, veintidós.
traps: Not 'diez y seis'.
Accents: dieciséis, veintidós, veintitrés, veintiséis.

topics.title: Numbers 30–199
topics.summary: Tens + y + units as separate words from 31: treinta y uno. cien = exactly 100; ciento + number above that, without y.
traps: 'ciento y treinta' is wrong.
Units come after tens, unlike German.

transfer.de: Order is tens then units: 45 = cuarenta y cinco.

topics.title: Hundreds and thousands
topics.summary: doscientos ... novecientos, irregular quinientos, setecientos, novecientos. Hundreds agree in gender: doscientas personas. mil is invariable: dos mil.
traps: Not 'cincocientos', 'sietecientos', 'nuevecientos'.
'un mil' is wrong for 1000.

topics.title: uno → un/una
topics.summary: Before a masculine noun uno becomes un (veintiún kilómetros); before a feminine noun una; standalone uno.
traps: 'treinta y uno años' is wrong.

topics.title: Telling the time
topics.summary: Es la una / Son las dos. y cuarto, y media, menos cuarto (of the next hour). a las + hour = at. ¿Qué hora es? / ¿A qué hora...?
examples: La reunión es a las diez y media.
traps: 'y media' is half past the current hour, unlike German 'halb neun' (= 8:30).
cuándo asks 'when' in general; '¿A qué hora?' asks the time.

transfer.de: halb neun = las ocho y media.

topics.title: Dates
topics.summary: el + cardinal number + de + month + de + year. Months lowercase. Only the 1st may be 'primero'.
examples: el veinticinco de octubre de dos mil veintiséis
Mi cumpleaños es el 25 de septiembre.
traps: Cardinal, not ordinal numbers: 'el dos de mayo'.
Months are not capitalised.

topics.title: Days of the week with the article
topics.summary: el sábado = on (this) Saturday, los sábados = on Saturdays; no preposition. 'Hoy es lunes' without article.
traps: 'en el sábado' is wrong.

transfer.de: am Samstag = el sábado, samstags = los sábados.

topics.title: Prices
topics.summary: ¿Cuánto cuesta / cuestan? ¿Cuánto es? Cuesta(n)... euros. 45,50 = cuarenta y cinco euros con cincuenta.
traps: 'y media' is only for time, not for prices.
No subject pronoun for things: 'Cuestan 30 euros'.

topics.title: Stress and written accents
topics.summary: Words ending in a vowel, -n or -s are stressed on the second-to-last syllable; others on the last. A written accent marks exceptions only. Antepenultimate stress always gets an accent.
traps: Hypercorrection: adding accents to every stressed syllable.
Only the acute accent exists (no à).

topics.title: Meaning-distinguishing accents
topics.summary: tú/tu, él/el, sí/si, mí/mi, está/esta, qué/que, cómo/como, porque/por qué.
traps: qué/cómo only in questions and exclamations, including indirect ones.

topics.title: estar for location
topics.summary: Where a known, specific thing or person is: estar + en / cerca de / al lado de...
traps: Events are an exception: 'El concierto es en el parque' (ser).

topics.title: hay vs estar
topics.summary: hay = there is/are (existence, new info, with un/una/numbers/no article). estar = where the known thing is (with el/la/proper names).
examples: El supermercado está en la esquina.
traps: 'Hay el banco' is wrong; 'Está un banco' is wrong.

topics.title: Prepositions of place
topics.summary: en, cerca de, lejos de, al lado de, delante de, detrás de, enfrente de, entre, encima de, debajo de.
examples: La farmacia está enfrente del banco.
traps: Compound prepositions need de, which contracts with el: 'al lado del hotel'.

topics.title: Contractions al and del
topics.summary: a + el = al, de + el = del. Not with la/los/las, and not with the pronoun él.
traps: 'a el' / 'de el' are wrong before the article.

topics.title: ir: present tense
topics.summary: voy, vas, va, vamos, vais, van + a + destination.
examples: Voy a la oficina en bici.
traps: 'yo va' — the third person form leaks into first person.

topics.title: a vs en
topics.summary: a = direction (to); en = location (in/at) and means of transport.
traps: 'Voy en casa' is wrong.

topics.title: Directions (fixed phrases)
topics.summary: Sigue recto, gira a la derecha / izquierda, toma la primera calle, está a cinco minutos. Learned as phrases before the imperative.
examples: Sigue recto y gira a la izquierda.
traps: Don't explain the imperative here; treat these as fixed phrases.

topics.title: Present tense: regular verbs
topics.summary: -ar: -o, -as, -a, -amos, -áis, -an. -er: -o, -es, -e, -emos, -éis, -en. -ir: -o, -es, -e, -imos, -ís, -en.
traps: yo always ends in -o except soy, estoy, voy, doy.
tú always ends in -s.

topics.title: Reflexive verbs
topics.summary: me, te, se, nos, os, se + verb. The pronoun goes before a conjugated verb or is attached to an infinitive.
traps: The pronoun is never dropped: '¿Te acuestas?'.
no goes before the pronoun: 'No me levanto'.

topics.title: Irregular yo forms
topics.summary: hago, pongo, salgo, traigo, conozco, sé, doy, veo, digo, vengo, tengo; the other persons are mostly regular.
examples: Salgo de casa a las ocho.
traps: 'hacio', 'salo' are wrong.

topics.title: estar + gerund
topics.summary: Action in progress right now: estar + -ando / -iendo. Irregular: leyendo, durmiendo, diciendo.
traps: Not used for the near future as in English: 'Mañana voy a trabajar', not 'Mañana estoy trabajando'.

topics.title: Frequency expressions
topics.summary: siempre, normalmente, a menudo, a veces, casi nunca, nunca, todos los días, una vez a la semana.
examples: Corro tres veces a la semana.
traps: 'nunca' after the verb needs no: 'No corro nunca' = 'Nunca corro'.

topics.title: antes de / después de + infinitive
topics.summary: Before/after doing something: antes de / después de + infinitive. después alone = afterwards.
traps: Infinitive, not a conjugated verb: 'después de corro' is wrong.

topics.title: Vowel change e → ie
topics.summary: The stressed e becomes ie in all forms except nosotros/vosotros: quiero, quieres, quiere, queremos, queréis, quieren. Also empezar, preferir, pensar, entender, tener, venir.
traps: 'queremos' keeps e because the stress moves.

topics.title: Vowel change o → ue
topics.summary: Stressed o becomes ue except in nosotros/vosotros: puedo, puedes, podemos. Also volver, dormir, costar, encontrar, acostarse. jugar: u → ue.
traps: 'puedemos' is wrong.

topics.title: Vowel change e → i
topics.summary: -ir verbs like pedir, repetir, servir, decir: pido, pides, pide, pedimos, pedís, piden.
traps: decir also has irregular yo: digo.

topics.title: ir vs venir
topics.summary: venir = come towards the speaker's location; ir = go elsewhere, including towards the listener. venir: vengo, vienes, viene, venimos, venís, vienen.
traps: Answering a call: 'Ya voy' (not 'Ya vengo').

topics.title: Basic connectors
topics.summary: y (e before i-), o (u before o-), pero, porque + indicative, también, tampoco, entonces.
examples: Me gusta mi trabajo porque aprendo mucho.
traps: porque (because) vs por qué (why).
porque takes the normal indicative: 'porque estoy cansado'.

topics.title: decir / pensar / creer + que
topics.summary: 'that' after verbs of saying and thinking is que and can't be dropped.
traps: Unlike German 'dass' or English 'that', que is mandatory.

topics.title: quisiera / me pone
topics.summary: Polite ordering: Quisiera..., ¿Me pone...?, Para mí..., Yo quiero... is acceptable in Spain. Learned as phrases, not as conditional.
traps: Don't explain the conditional here.

topics.title: Requests with ¿puede...? / ¿me trae...?
topics.summary: Ask for things or actions with a present-tense question: ¿Me trae la cuenta? ¿Puede cambiar...? ¿Tiene...?
traps: me/nos before the verb: '¿Me trae...?', not '¿Trae me...?'.

topics.title: Quantities
topics.summary: un poco de, mucho/a, demasiado/a, bastante, un kilo de, una botella de, medio kilo de, nada de. Containers and measures take de + noun without article.
traps: 'un kilo de los tomates' is wrong.

topics.title: estar + adjective for taste and food state
topics.summary: This specific dish: estar (Está rico, está frío). Food in general: ser (El chocolate es dulce).
traps: 'La paella es rica' sounds like a general statement.

topics.title: Demonstratives
topics.summary: este (here, near me), ese (near you / there), aquel (over there, far). Agree in gender and number; neuter esto, eso, aquello for unknown things.
examples: Este jersey es más barato que ese.
traps: Neuter esto/eso never refers to a known noun: 'esta camisa', not 'esto camisa'.

topics.title: Direct object pronouns
topics.summary: me, te, lo/la, nos, os, los/las replace the object; before the conjugated verb or attached to an infinitive.
traps: Gender follows the replaced noun.
Position: 'Lo compro', not 'Compro lo'.

topics.title: Comparatives
topics.summary: más / menos + adjective + que; tan + adjective + como. Irregular: mejor, peor, mayor, menor.
examples: Esta es más barata que esa.
Es tan caro como el otro.
traps: 'más bueno' → mejor.
que, not como, after más.

topics.title: otro, todo, cada, alguno
topics.summary: otro/a without un: 'otra talla'. todo el / toda la + noun. cada is invariable. alguno → algún before a masculine noun.
traps: 'una otra' is wrong.
'todo el día' needs the article.

topics.title: gustar and similar verbs
topics.summary: The thing liked is the subject: me gusta + singular/infinitive, me gustan + plural. The person is the indirect object me/te/le/nos/os/les. encantar, interesar, doler work the same way.
traps: Conjugating by person ('gusto', 'encantamos').
Missing article: 'Me gusta café'.

transfer.de: Works like gefallen: Der Film gefällt mir → Me gusta la película.

topics.title: Indirect object pronouns
topics.summary: me, te, le, nos, os, les = to/for someone. Often doubled with a + person: Le escribo a mi jefe.
examples: Le doy el libro a Ana.
traps: le vs lo: le = to him/her, lo = him/it.
Doubling with a + person is normal, not redundant.

topics.title: también / tampoco / a mí sí / a mí no
topics.summary: Agreeing: también (positive), tampoco (negative). Disagreeing: a mí sí / a mí no; with normal verbs: yo sí / yo no.
traps: With gustar use 'a mí', not 'yo': 'A mí también'.

topics.title: saber vs conocer
topics.summary: saber = know a fact / know how to (sé nadar). conocer = be acquainted with a person, place or thing (conozco Madrid).
traps: Personal a after conocer + person.
Ability: 'sé tocar la batería', not 'puedo'.

topics.title: ir a + infinitive
topics.summary: Near future and plans: only ir is conjugated, then a + one infinitive.
traps: 'va' for every person.
Conjugating the second verb: 'voy a tengo'.

topics.title: tener que + infinitive
topics.summary: Obligation: tener que + infinitive. 'hay que' = one has to (impersonal).
traps: Don't omit que: 'tengo trabajar' is wrong.

topics.title: Weather
topics.summary: hace calor/frío/sol/viento/buen tiempo; está nublado; hay niebla; llueve, nieva; está lloviendo.
traps: 'Es frío' about the weather is wrong.

topics.title: Making and answering proposals
topics.summary: ¿Quedamos...? ¿Por qué no...? ¿Te viene bien...? Vale. Perfecto. Lo siento, no puedo. ¿Y si...?
examples: Lo siento, el viernes no puedo. ¿Y el sábado?
traps: quedar = arrange to meet in Spain.

topics.title: Real conditions: si + present
topics.summary: si + present, present / ir a / imperative for real conditions. si (if) has no accent; sí (yes) does.
traps: No future after si: 'si lloverá' is wrong.

topics.title: Preterite: recognising forms
topics.summary: Recognise preterite forms in texts before producing them: -é/-ó endings, fue, hizo, tuvo.
examples: Ayer fui al cine y compré palomitas.
traps: compro (I buy) vs compró (he bought): the accent changes person and tense.

topics.title: Preterite: regular -ar verbs
topics.summary: -é, -aste, -ó, -amos, -asteis, -aron. Spelling: -gar → -gué, -car → -qué, -zar → -cé in yo.
traps: nosotros form equals present: trabajamos (context decides).
Missing accent on -é/-ó.

topics.title: Preterite: regular -er/-ir verbs
topics.summary: -í, -iste, -ió, -imos, -isteis, -ieron. leer/creer: leyó, leyeron.
traps: vivimos = present and past.

topics.title: Preterite of ser and ir
topics.summary: ser and ir share the same forms: fui, fuiste, fue, fuimos, fuisteis, fueron. No written accents.
traps: 'fuí', 'fué' with accents are wrong.

topics.title: Preterite: irregular stems
topics.summary: Stem + -e, -iste, -o, -imos, -isteis, -ieron, no accents: hice/hizo, tuve, estuve, pude, puse, vine, quise, supe; dije/dijeron, traje/trajeron.
traps: hizo with z.
dijeron, not 'dijieron'.

topics.title: Past time markers
topics.summary: ayer, anoche, anteayer, el lunes pasado, la semana pasada, el año pasado, en 2019, hace dos días.
examples: Hace tres años corrí un maratón.
traps: hace + time = ago, placed before: 'hace dos días'.

topics.title: por vs para
topics.summary: para: purpose, recipient, destination, deadline. por: cause, through/along, exchange/price, means, duration, 'per'.
traps: Purpose + infinitive is para: 'para aprender'.
'gracias por', never 'para'.

topics.title: Travel prepositions
topics.summary: en tren/avión/coche, a pie, en bici; de ... a ...; desde ... hasta ...; salir de, llegar a.
examples: Fui de Leipzig a Madrid en avión.
Llegamos a Sevilla por la noche.
traps: 'llegar en' a city is wrong: llegar a.

topics.title: Preterite: -ir stem changes
topics.summary: -ir verbs with a present stem change also change in él/ellos: pidió, pidieron, durmió, durmieron, prefirió.
examples: Dormimos poco, pero ellos durmieron bien.
traps: Only 3rd person changes: pedí, pediste, pidió.

topics.title: Present perfect (pretérito perfecto)
topics.summary: haber (he, has, ha, hemos, habéis, han) + participle (-ado, -ido). Participle never agrees, nothing goes between haber and participle.
traps: Always haber, never ser, even where German uses sein: 'He ido', not 'Soy ido'.

topics.title: Irregular participles
topics.summary: hecho, dicho, visto, escrito, puesto, vuelto, abierto, roto, muerto, descubierto.
examples: Todavía no he escrito el informe.
traps: 'hacido', 'escribido', 'vido' are wrong.

topics.title: ya / todavía no / alguna vez / nunca
topics.summary: ya = already, todavía no / aún no = not yet, alguna vez = ever, nunca = never; typical with the present perfect.
traps: 'todavía' alone means still: 'Todavía trabajo aquí'.

topics.variety_note: es-ES: perfecto for today/this week/unfinished period; Latin America mostly uses the preterite there.
topics.title: Perfecto vs indefinido (Spain)
topics.summary: In Spain: perfecto for time periods that are not over (hoy, esta semana, este año) and experiences; indefinido for finished periods (ayer, el año pasado).
traps: 'Ayer he ido' is wrong in standard Spanish.

topics.title: Imperfect (pretérito imperfecto)
topics.summary: -aba, -abas, -aba, -ábamos, -abais, -aban; -ía, -ías, -ía, -íamos, -íais, -ían. Only 3 irregular: ser (era), ir (iba), ver (veía). Past habits and descriptions.
traps: Accent on -ábamos and on every -ía form.

topics.title: soler + infinitive
topics.summary: Habitual action: suelo correr por la mañana; past habit: solía.
examples: Suelo trabajar desde casa los viernes.
traps: soler is followed directly by the infinitive, no preposition.

topics.title: Indefinido vs imperfecto: basics
topics.summary: Imperfect: background, description, habits, ongoing actions. Indefinido: completed events that move the story forward.
traps: Duration doesn't decide: 'Viví diez años en Moscú' (completed) is indefinido.

transfer.ru: Похоже на несовершенный/совершенный вид, но не совпадает полностью: «жил десять лет» = viví.

topics.title: me duele / me duelen
topics.summary: Pain works like gustar: Me duele la cabeza, me duelen las piernas. Body parts take the definite article, not a possessive.
examples: Me duele la rodilla desde el maratón.
traps: 'Mi cabeza duele' is unnatural.
Article, not possessive: 'la rodilla'.

topics.title: Symptoms with tener and estar
topics.summary: tengo fiebre / tos / gripe / dolor de...; estoy resfriado / mareado; desde hace + time.
examples: Tengo fiebre desde hace dos días.
traps: desde hace, not 'desde' alone, for a period.

topics.title: Advice: deber, hay que, es mejor
topics.summary: deber + infinitive (should), hay que + infinitive (one must), es mejor / es importante + infinitive.
traps: 'debes de' means probability, not obligation.

topics.title: Affirmative imperative (tú)
topics.summary: Regular = 3rd person singular present: habla, come, escribe. Irregular: ven, ve, haz, di, pon, sal, ten, sé. vosotros: -ad/-ed/-id.
traps: Negative commands use a different form (subjunctive), not covered at A2 production level.

topics.title: Imperative with pronouns
topics.summary: Pronouns attach to the affirmative imperative; the stress stays put, so an accent is often added: dímelo, tráelo, siéntate.
traps: Missing accent: 'damelo' → dámelo.

topics.title: Double object pronouns
topics.summary: Indirect before direct: me lo, te la. le/les becomes se before lo/la/los/las: se lo doy.
examples: Se lo he dicho a Marta.
traps: 'le lo' is wrong → se lo.

topics.title: estar + participle for states
topics.summary: Resulting state: está roto / cerrado / abierto / apagado; participle agrees like an adjective.
traps: Agreement: 'la ventana está abierta'.

topics.title: Stressed possessives: mío, tuyo
topics.summary: mío, tuyo, suyo, nuestro, vuestro — after ser or the noun, and as pronouns with the article: el mío.
examples: Mi piso es más pequeño que el tuyo.
traps: Agree with the possessed thing: 'Esta llave es mía'.

topics.title: me gustaría / podría / ¿podrías...?
topics.summary: Polite wishes and requests as fixed phrases before the conditional is taught: Me gustaría..., ¿Podrías...?, ¿Podríamos...?
traps: Don't explain the conditional paradigm here.

topics.title: Simple future
topics.summary: Infinitive + -é, -ás, -á, -emos, -éis, -án. Irregular stems: har-, tendr-, podr-, saldr-, vendr-, dir-, sabr-, pondr-, querr-.
traps: In speech ir a + infinitive is more common for plans.

topics.title: Discourse connectors
topics.summary: así que, por eso, además, aunque, sin embargo, primero, luego, al final.
examples: Estoy enfermo, así que no puedo ir.
traps: aunque + indicative for facts; the subjunctive case is not taught at A2.

topics.title: Superlatives
topics.summary: el/la/los/las + más/menos + adjective + de; mejor/peor. Absolute: -ísimo (carísimo).
examples: Es la ciudad más bonita de España.
Es el mejor restaurante del barrio.
traps: 'de', not 'en': 'el más alto de la clase'.

topics.title: Comparing quantities
topics.summary: tanto/a/os/as + noun + como; más/menos + noun + que; más de / menos de + number.
examples: No tengo tanto tiempo como antes.
traps: Before a number: más de, not más que.

topics.title: Giving opinions
topics.summary: Creo que..., Me parece que..., Para mí..., En mi opinión..., (No) estoy de acuerdo con..., Tienes razón.
examples: Me parece que la segunda opción es mejor.
traps: 'Estoy de acuerdo', not 'Soy de acuerdo'.

topics.title: Conditional for politeness
topics.summary: Infinitive + -ía, -ías, -ía, -íamos, -íais, -ían, same irregular stems as the future. Polite requests and wishes.
traps: Same stems as the future: 'tendría', not 'tenería'.

topics.title: Reported speech: basics
topics.summary: Dice que + same tense; Me dijo que + present for things still true. Questions: Me preguntó si / dónde...
examples: El recepcionista dijo que la habitación está lista.
traps: Tense backshift is not required at A2 when the fact still holds.

topics.title: Negative words: nadie, nada, ninguno
topics.summary: After the verb they need no: No vino nadie. Before the verb no 'no': Nadie vino. ninguno → ningún before a masculine noun.
traps: Double negation is required, unlike German/English.
ninguno is almost always singular.

transfer.ru: Двойное отрицание как в русском: «никто не пришёл» = No vino nadie.

topics.title: Narrating in the past
topics.summary: Combine imperfect (scene, background) and indefinido (events) in a connected story.
examples: Era 2019, vivía en Leipzig y trabajaba mucho. Un día decidí correr un maratón.
traps: Telling a whole story in imperfect or in indefinido only.

topics.title: Time expressions in stories
topics.summary: cuando + past, mientras + imperfect, al + infinitive, hace + time (ago), desde hace + time (for, still ongoing), hace ... que.
examples: Vivo en Alemania desde hace quince años.
Al llegar, llamé a mi madre.
traps: Ongoing state: present + desde hace, not a past tense.

transfer.de: seit 15 Jahren = desde hace quince años (present tense, as in German).

topics.title: Relative clauses: que, donde
topics.summary: que for people and things, donde for places; lo que = what (the thing that).
examples: La empresa donde trabajo es pequeña.
Lo que más me gusta es correr.
traps: 'el que' / 'quien' are not needed at A2 for basic clauses.

error_defs.text: Missing, extra or wrong written accent/diacritic.
Wrong or unknown word; meaning confused.
Wrong grammatical gender of a noun.
Adjective/article/pronoun doesn't agree in gender or number.
Article missing, extra or wrong type (definite/indefinite).
Right tense, wrong verb form (person, number, stem).
Grammatically fine but wrong register or politeness level.
